phase_0.boundary_condition: The unit cycle {1} acts as the terminal anchor where all trajectories converge or loop, defining the closed boundary of the Collatz state space.

⊢.justification: The system begins with an uninitialized natural number n ≥ 1, representing the void state before parity evaluation.

⊣.justification: The value 1 forms the closed boundary; reaching 1 implies entry into the 1→1 loop, the terminal anchor of the system.

≻.justification: The transformation (3n+1)/2 for odd n represents the forward morphism, increasing magnitude and moving away from the anchor.

≺.justification: The transformation n/2 for even n represents the reverse morphism, decreasing magnitude and descending toward the anchor.

⋈.justification: Sequential application of the Collatz map composes multiple steps into a single trajectory path.

⊙.justification: The state n=1 is self-referential; col(1)=1, meaning the element recognizes itself as the identity of the loop.

∈.justification: The system splits into two distinct arms based on the parity of n: the odd arm (expansion) and the even arm (contraction).

∋.justification: The arms rejoin at the next integer state; conflicting paths (expansion vs contraction) fuse into a single resolved trajectory step.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where the trajectory strictly decreases (col^k(n) < n), confirming progress toward the anchor.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the trajectory increases (col(n) > n), representing a temporary divergence from the anchor.

⊞.justification: The state where n ≡ 3 (mod 4) holds both expansion potential (odd) and immediate contraction potential (next step even), a paradice of simultaneous opposing forces.

⊡.justification: The permanent record of the step count k where the trajectory first reaches 1, an irreversible fixation of the stopping time.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: An arbitrary natural number n ≥ 1 before any Collatz operation is applied.
phase_3.true_description: The trajectory has contracted (col^k(n) < n) or reached the unit cycle.
phase_3.false_description: The trajectory has expanded (col(n) > n) in the current step.
phase_3.both_description: A state n ≡ 3 (mod 4) where the immediate step expands but the subsequent step contracts, holding both expansion and contraction potentials simultaneously.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the system with an arbitrary natural number n ≥ 1.
Branch the trajectory based on the parity of n.
Execute the odd expansion morphism (3n+1)/2 on the T-arm.
Affirm the expansion state where magnitude increases.
Execute the even contraction morphism n/2 on the F-arm.
Affirm the contraction state where magnitude decreases.
Rejoin the parity arms into the next integer state.
Compose the current step with the previous trajectory history.
Branch again based on the parity of the new state.
Apply odd expansion if the new state is odd.
Record the affirmative expansion.
Apply even contraction if the new state is even.
Record the negative contraction.
Fuse the arms to produce the subsequent state.
Hold the modular residue state n ≡ 3 (mod 4) where expansion and contraction coexist.
Chain the modular residue evaluation into the trajectory.
Split the trajectory for the 8m+3 case analysis.
Apply the 3-step expansion sequence for 8m+3.
Verify the expansion to 9m+4.
Apply the subsequent contraction steps.
Verify the contraction to a value less than input.
Fuse the 8m+3 analysis into a single contraction verdict.
Split the trajectory for the 8m+7 case analysis.
Apply the expansion sequence for 8m+7.
Verify the expansion to 27m+26.
Apply the contraction sequence.
Verify the contraction to a value less than input.
Fuse the 8m+7 analysis into a single contraction verdict.
Compose the 8m+3 and 8m+7 contraction proofs.
Recognize the fixed point n=1 where col(1)=1.
Affirm the termination condition at n=1.
Record the stopping time k as a permanent, append-only fact.
Close the system at the unit cycle boundary.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The parity check function that translates integer n into the appropriate morphism (3n+1)/2 or n/2.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The integer value passed sequentially between iterations of the Collatz map.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The trajectory history stored as a sequence of integers leading to the current state.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The deterministic rule that selects the next operation based solely on the parity of the current integer.
phase_5.alfs_store: The set of lemmas proving contraction for n ≡ 3 (mod 4) and n ≡ 7 (mod 8) as the canonical reference for convergence.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One bit of parity information consumed per operation cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: An integer n with unknown trajectory length.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: An integer col(n) with one step of trajectory history recorded.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The system is deterministic and reversible in principle (given the full trajectory), conserving information while reducing magnitude on average.
